requirement:
HC's FIXME review uses an agent criterion to assess whether each linked issue's
title and opening post describe the FIXME's acknowledged gap. It selects the
FIXME's tracking-issue edges through the SDK's tracked interface and supplies
the FIXME and selected issue contents through tracked reads or ask insertions.

A completed assessment that an issue is unrelated fails that issue's relevance
check.
rationale:
The tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes.related`. I did not read the implementation source.

**Agent criterion judges each linked issue.** `src/sdk/issues.rs#mod[tests]/fn[relevance_reviews_each_linked_issue_using_tracked_issue_and_fixme_contents]` links two issues to one FIXME. A scripted model returns one related and one unrelated judgment. The test asserts that the output holds exactly `[(ISSUE, true), (other, false)]`, so each issue is judged separately.

**FIXME and issue contents are supplied.** The same test asserts that the prompt contains the FIXME text ("An assertion for readiness is missing"). It also asserts that the prompt contains the title and opening post of both linked issues.

**Tracking-issue edges are selected through the tracked interface.** The test asserts that the verified dependencies include `Dependency::OutgoingEdges(fixme, TrackingIssue, _)`. It also asserts `Dependency::Node` entries, with fingerprints, for the FIXME and both issue nodes. Those are the tracked reads. When an issue's title changes, `check_inputs` returns false, which shows the contents are tracked inputs.

**An unrelated verdict fails that issue's relevance check.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_persists_a_manual_correction_and_the_tracking_inputs_for_an_unrelated_issue]` runs the full `author` flow with two issues. The agent marks #125 unrelated and #126 related. The test asserts these results:
- The determination is false.
- Exactly one manual correction exists, it names #125 and not #126, and its rationale is the model's reason.
- The reason appears in stderr.

The flow therefore fails only the unrelated issue. The same test asserts that the second request's prompt includes the FIXME acknowledgment text and the issue title and opening post. It also asserts that the persisted dependencies include the FIXME node, both issue nodes, and the `TrackingIssue` outgoing edges.

Together the two tests cover the related and unrelated outcomes and the per-issue handling. I found no gaps.
